channel.title: Blowhorn Resources: Tips and tricks
channel.description: Everything in Blowhorn Resources tagged Tips and tricks.

item.title: Review the week, not the post
item.description: Single posts are noise. A five-minute weekly review of your activities - success rate, posting times, failure reasons - is where the signal lives, and it is the habit behind every account that keeps improving.

item.title: A platform limit is information, not an error
item.description: When a platform slows or refuses your posts, it is telling you the current price of attention. The right response is a smaller, slower run - never a faster retry.

item.title: Read the failure before you retry
item.description: Every failed post carries its reason, and the reason names the fix. Retrying without reading it repeats the same failure at the same target, and teaches the platform you are not paying attention.

item.title: Post at your audience's hour, not yours
item.description: Write whenever you think clearly; post when your readers are actually scrolling. Scheduling exists to separate those two moments, and a one-hour shift in posting time is the cheapest experiment in this whole series.

item.title: Start every new troop on approval
item.description: Turn on approval for a new troop's first runs. You see each post before it goes out, catch the targeting and wording mistakes while they are still free, then let it run on its own.

item.title: Space the queue, not the burst
item.description: If a troop's posts all land inside a few minutes, widen the spacing before you touch anything else. Bursts are the pattern platforms notice, and spacing is the one setting that fixes the shape of a whole run.
